extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants (practitioners preparing or examining patent specifications)
extracted.subtask_short: US patent specification form and content
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and examiner guidance for the content, format, paper/electronic submission, and procedural handling of U.S. patent specifications, claims, abstracts, drawings, and associated materials under 35 U.S.C. §112 and 37 CFR (e.g., 1.52, 1.71, 1.58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description and enablement (37 CFR 1.71(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must include a written description of the invention and of the manner and process of making and using the same, in such full, clear, concise, and exact terms as to enable any person skilled in the art to make and use the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a newly filed application obviously fails to disclose the invention with the clarity required by 35 U.S.C. 112, revision should be required. Examiner should object where the specification is not enabling and request revision (see MPEP § 702.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification must set forth precise invention and best mode (37 CFR 1.71(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must set forth the precise invention sought to be patented, distinguish it from other inventions and the prior art, describe a complete specific embodiment, explain the mode of operation or principle when applicable, and set forth the best mode contemplated by the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description should be complete for a specific embodiment; include mode of operation when applicable; ensure best mode disclosure to avoid statutory issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement-specific description (37 CFR 1.71(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: For an improvement, the specification must particularly point out the part(s) of the process, machine, manufacture, composition of matter to which the improvement relates and be confined to the specific improvement and necessary cooperating parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit description to the improvement and parts that necessarily cooperate with it to avoid unrelated disclosure or overbroad descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on unrelated material in written description
rubrics_metrics.description: The written description must not include information that is not related to applicant's invention (e.g., prospective disclaimers regarding comments made by examiners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unrelated information is included, the examiner will object and require applicant to cancel or otherwise correct that information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification sheet separation and section placement (37 CFR 1.71(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must commence on a separate sheet; each sheet including part of the specification may not include other parts of the application. The claim(s), abstract, and sequence listing (if any) should not be included on a sheet including any other part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each of these sections (specification, abstract, claims, sequence listings) should begin on a new page because they are separately indexed in the Image File Wrapper; avoid overlap of sections on a single page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must commence on separate sheet/page (37 CFR 1.75(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim or claims must commence on a separate physical sheet or electronic page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims are not printed on the same page as other application sections; when filing electronically, ensure claim page separation in the electronic document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract must commence on separate sheet/page (37 CFR 1.72(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract must commence on a separate physical sheet or electronic page (or be the first page of the patent in reissue applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts should not share a page with other parts of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement and non-English filings (37 CFR 1.52(b)/(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be in the English language or accompanied by an English translation and a statement that the translation is accurate. Nonprovisional applications filed in a non-English language require an English translation, a statement of accuracy, and the processing fee; provisional applications filed in another language do not require translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required items are not filed, applicant will be notified and given time to file them to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for British English spellings
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should not object merely because applicants use British English spellings rather than American English; 37 CFR 1.52(b)(1)(ii) requires only that the application be in the English language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No requirement to replace British spellings with American spellings in U.S. applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper quality and characteristics (37 CFR 1.52(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers (other than drawings) to become part of the permanent USPTO records must be on sheets of paper the same size, flexible, strong, smooth, non-shiny, durable, and white.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable reproduction methods: typed, mimeographed, xeroprinted, multigraphed, or nonsmearing carbon copies are acceptable. Avoid so-called 'easily erasable' paper or heat-sensitive duplications which are unsatisfactory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper size and margins (37 CFR 1.52(a)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper size must be either 21.0 x 29.7 cm (A4) or 21.6 x 27.9 cm (8.5 x 11 inches). Each sheet (other than drawings) must include a top margin of at least 2.0 cm, left side margin at least 2.5 cm, right side margin at least 2.0 cm, and bottom margin at least 2.0 cm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application papers should all be the same size; if not, USPTO will require substitute papers that comply. See 37 CFR 1.84 for drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-side printing and portrait orientation (37 CFR 1.52(a)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be written on only one side in portrait orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit pages with printing on both sides or landscape pages except where specifically allowed (e.g., some formulae/tables).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legible, permanent printing and contrast (37 CFR 1.52(a)(1)(iv) & general guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be plainly and legibly written by typewriter or machine printer in permanent dark ink (sufficient clarity and contrast to permit direct reproduction and OCR). Legibility includes ability to be photocopied, photomicrographed and electronically reproduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gray lines or backgrounds reduce reproduction quality; if papers are not of required quality, substitute typewritten or mechanically printed papers will be required. If erasures remove imprint, examiner should require substitute copies or USPTO-made copies at applicant expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line spacing, font, and column requirements (37 CFR 1.52(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification (including claims and abstract) must have lines that are 1.5 or double spaced; text in a nonscript type font (e.g., Arial, Times Roman, or Courier), preferably font size 12; capital letters at least 0.3175 cm high but no smaller than 0.21 cm; and only a single column of text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text may not be written solely in capital letters. Use readable font sizes; examiners may object for spacing or numerous errors (form paragraphs 6.29–6.31).

rubrics_metrics.name: Page and paragraph numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Pages of the specification including claims and abstract must be consecutively numbered starting with 1, with numbers centrally located above or preferably below the text. Paragraphs (other than claims or abstract) may be numbered at filing using four numerals in square brackets (e.g., [0001]) with leading zeros and bold brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nontext elements are considered part of the surrounding paragraph and should not be independently numbered. Section headers are not considered paragraphs and should not be numbered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alterations and interlineations rules (37 CFR 1.52(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interlineation, erasure, cancellation, or other alteration must be made before signing any accompanying oath or declaration, and should be dated and initialed or signed on the same sheet. Application papers containing alterations made after signing the oath must be supported by a supplemental oath or declaration under § 1.67. After signing, amendments may only be made as provided by § 1.121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict enforcement; if an oath is copied from a prior application, some later alterations are permitted provided they do not introduce new matter relative to the prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact disc and electronic medium submission rules (37 CFR 1.52(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic documents (e.g., computer program listings, sequence listings) may be submitted on CD-ROM or CD-R in compliance with specified formatting and labeling rules. CDs must be finalized (CD-R), conform to ISO 9660, use ASCII for contents, and be accompanied by a paper transmittal letter listing machine format, OS compatibility, file names, sizes, creation dates, and any special information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CDs submitted in duplicate (Copy 1 and Copy 2) unless only containing a sequence listing; replacement CDs must be labeled with replacement date. If copies differ, the Office uses 'Copy 1'; unreadable files on both copies are treated as not submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact disc labeling content
rubrics_metrics.description: Each compact disc must be labeled with: name of each inventor (if known); title of the invention; docket or application number (if known); creation date of the CD; order indicator if multiple discs; indication that the disk is 'Copy 1' or 'Copy 2'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmittal letter must state that the two CDs are identical. If files are unreadable or in noncompliant format, treated as not submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission fee sizing and paper-equivalents (counting) (37 CFR 1.52(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence listings and computer program listings submitted electronically in compliance with §§ 1.52(e), 1.821(c)/(e), and 1.96 may be excluded when determining the application size fee. Content submitted on electronic medium may be counted in three-kilobyte units as equivalent to sheets of paper for fee calculations; for EFS submissions, a 75% factor may apply when rendered into the IFW for size-fee purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the detailed rules for excluding certain electronic files and how to count bytes toward application size fee (see § 1.16(s) and § 1.492(j)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical and mathematical formulae and tables rules (37 CFR 1.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification may contain chemical and mathematical formulae and tables (but not drawings or flow diagrams). Tables in both drawings and description are allowed only if the application was filed under 35 U.S.C. 371. Claims may contain tables if necessary to conform to 35 U.S.C. 112 or if otherwise desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables submitted electronically must maintain spatial relationships; formulae must be encoded to preserve character positioning. Formulae/tables may be placed in landscape if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font size and spacing for formulae and tables (37 CFR 1.58(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Typewritten characters in formulae and tables must be from a nonscript font with capital letters at least 0.422 cm (0.166 inch) high (preferably font size 12) but may be no smaller than 0.21 cm. Provide a space at least 0.64 cm (1/4 inch) between complex formulae/tables and text. Tables should have lines/columns closely spaced consistent with legibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If tables are longer than 50 pages or total tables exceed 100 pages, submit tables electronically or follow special handling. Nontext elements that extend to left margin should not be independently paragraph-numbered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listings and program listings separate-handling guidance (37 CFR 1.821/1.96 references)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence listings and computer program listings filed in electronic medium in compliance with applicable sections are treated specially (e.g., excluded from size-fee counting in some cases) and must be incorporated by reference into the specification with identifying information (file names, creation dates, sizes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may require amendment to include on-paper any part previously on a compact disc; compact disc material must be identified in a separate paragraph with file names, dates, and sizes (§ 1.77(b)(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application papers must be same size and unbound
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers that are to become part of the permanent record must be on sheets of paper that are the same size and not permanently bound together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment should not have two different paper sizes; however, the specification and drawings may be different sizes relative to each other. Noncompliant papers will prompt a 'Notice to File Corrected Application Papers'.

rubrics_metrics.name: No holes in submitted sheets (37 CFR 1.52(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted on paper or by facsimile that are to become part of the permanent records should have no holes in the sheets as submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid punching holes prior to submission; USPTO scanning and image processing expects plain sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies and substitute papers for noncompliant submissions (37 CFR 1.125 and related guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: If papers filed do not comply with 37 CFR 1.52, the Office will mail a Notice to File Corrected Application Papers setting a time to correct deficiencies. Substitute typewritten or mechanically printed papers of suitable quality will be required; substitute papers filed after the filing date are not treated as the original disclosure for certified copy or priority purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO may perform exception processing to scan noncompliant papers but certified copies may remain illegible; applicants should file substitutes to ensure legible IFW records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Easily erasable paper and unsatisfactory reproduction processes (¶ 6.32 guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper that is easily erasable (special coating) or reproductions prepared by heat-sensitive, hectographic, or spirit duplication processes are not satisfactory as permanent copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If light pressure of an eraser removes imprints, require applicant to submit permanent copies or order a USPTO-made photocopy at applicant expense for incorporation in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legibility standard and examiner actions (¶ 6.32.01 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification and any amendments must be plainly and legibly written in a nonscript font with specified minimum sizes, single column, and sufficient contrast to allow photographic and electronic reproduction and OCR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If illegible, a legible substitute specification complying with 37 CFR 1.52(a)/(b) and 1.125 is required. Use form paragraphs (e.g., 6.32) to object to nonpermanent or illegible papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of metric (SI) units recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should use metric (S.I.) units followed by equivalent English units when describing dimensions to minimize future conversion necessity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present metric units first (S.I.) and include English equivalents in parentheses or following text where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright/mask work notices and required authorization text (37 CFR 1.71(d)-(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may be placed adjacent to such material in a design or utility patent application, limited to elements provided for by law, and inclusion is permitted only if the specified authorization language (a paragraph stating that facsimile reproduction by anyone of the patent document is permitted but other copyright/mask rights are reserved) is included at the beginning of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of properly limited notices: '©1983 John Doe' or '*M* John Doe'. The authorization paragraph should preferably be the first paragraph of the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of parties to joint research agreement (35 U.S.C. 103(c)(2)(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification may disclose or be amended to disclose the names of parties to a joint research agreement. Amendments to add such names must be accompanied by a processing fee if not filed within specified time periods (e.g., within three months of filing date or before the first office action on the merits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If names are added after issue fee payment, the issued patent may not include them; correction requires a certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and § 1.323.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs to object to minor informalities and spacing/errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.29 may be used where disclosure contains minor informalities (spelling errors, inconsistent terminology, numbering of elements). Form paragraphs 6.28–6.32 should be used where appropriate, including objects for spacing of lines, numerous errors, or illegible/erasable paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified form paragraphs to identify and request correction of informalities and to guide applicant corrections.
